65:62.name: Kicker
65:62.description: Post type label. Text is bound to type/label, so it reads the card's Post Type mode; no text property needed.

65:65.name: Check Row

Label.default: Wired the tokens into the site shell

65:65.description: One line of a Ledger or Before / After card. Check (type ink) for shipped, Cross (error) for the mistake, Dot for a note. Struck=Yes is the subtraction ledger, what was cut: the text drops to on-surface-variant and a 3px on-surface-variant strike runs exactly the length of the text, its own layer (.jk-row__strike). Real item names at uneven lengths; 6 rows at most.

65:86.name: Token Chip
65:86.description: A component or token chip for Architecture Diagram zones and Pipeline outputs. Override the swatch fill with the real token.

65:89.name: Arrow
65:89.description: One arrow per card. The annotation carries the rule. A diagram that needs two arrows is two cards.

65:94.name: Equals Badge
65:94.description: The whole argument of a Parity card. Sits on the hairline between the Figma half and the code half.

65:96.name: Terminal
65:96.description: The hero of a Pipeline card: one real command. Content never invents: use the command that actually ran.

65:99.name: Zone Label
65:99.description: Sits on the top edge of a dashed zone (absolute, y = -18). Names the zone: PRIMITIVES, FIGMA, BEFORE…

36:31.name: Tag
36:31.description: A short uppercase label chip. .lk-tag. Used in a wrapping row of 4px gaps (profile tags, Link Row tags).

36:33.name: Icon Kicker
36:33.description: Category label above a row or tile title: a 16px icon in a 4px box, then a mono uppercase label in scrim at 80%. .lk-kicker. Studio uses the Command glyph; Blog Feather; Shop and Support Layout Grid.

36:50.name: Pill Button
36:50.description: Header link (Ghost) and Follow (Outlined). Mono 11px, full radius. .lk-header__link, .lk-follow. Hover: Ghost takes surface-container-lowest at 40%, Outlined surface-container-high. Focus draws a 2px primary ring (:focus-visible). Ghost hides below 640px in the header.

36:67.name: Icon Button
36:67.description: 32px round button on inverse-surface; the icon takes inverse-on-surface. Social: 18px icon (.lk-social). Go: 20px chevron at the end of a Link Row (.lk-row__go). Hover lifts to primary (on a Link Row, hovering the row lifts its Go). Needs an aria-label in code (the social kind).

36:96.name: Tab
36:96.description: Filter tab: a toggle button (aria-pressed), 46px tall, 10px radius, comic lettering. .lk-tab. Hover takes surface-container-lowest at 40%; Selected sits on surface-container-lowest with an outline; Focus draws a 2px primary ring. Fills its grid cell (FILL width) in a row of five.

36:107.name: Avatar
36:107.description: Round profile photo with a 1px on-surface ring over tertiary-98 (shown when there is no photo). Large 172px; Compact 120px below 640px. .lk-avatar. Photo fill: Imagery/Portrait.

203:2.name: Stamp and Postmark
203:2.description: The post type's stamp, cancelled (catalog: cachet). A perforated stamp in type/accent with the type's icon (Flag progress, Signpost decision, Skull failure, Sun principle, Bell teaching), its label and the 2¢ value from Entry 001-C; a ring postmark with the handle or series over the day or date, the card's topic glyph, and five machine waves. Ink is on-surface at 62%. Code adds speckled wear (an SVG noise mask) that Figma doesn't draw. 400×220. Edit the ring text on the curve directly (text on a path takes no component property). Sample: the figma-variables card. Dressing.tsx Cachet (@jkidd/react).

205:6.name: Rubber Stamp
205:6.description: One verdict word the card itself says (catalog: rubber), boxed twice in type/ink at 80% and tilted 4–10°; the code sizes it 64 + 34px a letter by 92. Only when the card has a verdict. Code adds speckled wear that Figma doesn't draw. Sample: the link-page-weight card. Dressing.tsx RubberStamp (@jkidd/react).

205:10.name: Divider Imprint
205:10.description: The divided back's centre rule (catalog: imprint), with the card's source printed up it like a publisher's number: IDEA <id> · JOURNAL <event>, in on-surface-variant at 70%. Only when the card has a source. Sample: the figma-variables card. Dressing.tsx Imprint (@jkidd/react).

205:16.name: Registration Mark
205:16.description: A crosshair target, the printer's mark (catalog: registration): one in each corner, 24px in from the edges and the rail, in on-surface at 45%, for a build that runs through a press. Dressing.tsx Target (@jkidd/react).

205:19.name: Colour Bar
205:19.description: The five post type accents as a printer's colour bar along the foot of the card (catalog: colorbar), centred 17px up: each swatch is type/accent fixed to its own Post Type mode, so it shows all five whatever the card's type. dressing.css .jk-back__colorbar (@jkidd/ui).

205:33.name: Photo Corner
205:33.description: Album corners on each zone, so two halves sit like mounted prints (catalog: corners): on-surface at 82%, set 6px out from the zone's corners. Parity cards. Dressing.tsx PhotoCorners (@jkidd/react).

205:13.name: Airmail Edge
205:13.description: Bands of type/accent and on-surface chevrons along the top and bottom edges (catalog: airmail), 14px tall from the rail to the right edge, at 85%: one dispatch in a run, so only on series posts. Stretch it to the card's width; it clips. dressing.css .jk-back__airmail (@jkidd/ui).

215:33.name: Graph Paper
215:33.description: Graph paper (catalog: grid): a 24px minor grid at 9% and a 120px major grid at 20%, in type/accent, so it takes the card's Post Type mode; the stage postcards' paper. A texture: lay it over the stock, under the content, one per card. Resize it to the card (it clips; drawn to 1600×1350). Code: back.css [data-texture=grid].

215:36.name: Ledger Ruling
215:36.description: Ledger ruling (catalog: ledger): feint rules every 56px in on-surface at 9% and a double margin line at 96px and 104px in type/accent at 14%, left of the content. A texture for Ledger cards: lay it over the stock, under the content. Resize it to the card (it clips; drawn to 1600×1350). Code: back.css [data-texture=ledger].
